parts.latex: Which of the following best represents the graph of $y=10(0.8)^x$?

solutions.latex:
When $x = 0$, $y = 10(0.8)^0 = 10$, so the $y$-intercept is $10$.

The base $0.8$ is between $0$ and $1$, so $y$ decreases as $x$ increases, approaching $0$.

Graph A is the decreasing exponential with $y$-intercept $10$.

parts.latex: Which of the following best represents the graph of $y=10(3^x)$?

solutions.latex:
At $x=0$:
$$y=10(3^0)=10$$
All four curves are increasing exponentials with horizontal asymptote $y=0$, so the graph is the one with $y$-intercept 10.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{347_q29_s1}

When $x=0$:

$$\begin{aligned} y &= 3e^{0}+1 \\ &= 4 \end{aligned}$$

As $x\to\infty$, $e^{-x}\to 0$, so $y=1$ is a horizontal asymptote.
